items.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
items.summary: After Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge said Claude helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis, two independent groups have now checked the claim and say it holds up. The hypothesis has resisted proof for over 150 years and is one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems.
items.why_it_matters: Independent verification turns a disputed AI claim into one of the strongest documented cases of an AI system contributing to a major mathematical breakthrough.

items.title: Thinking Machines wows with Inkling 2 Mini looped transformer model that runs locally on laptops
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab, the startup led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights multimodal looped-transformer model designed to run offline on a 32GB MacBook Pro or a single desktop GPU rather than in the cloud.
items.why_it_matters: A capable multimodal model that runs on consumer laptop hardware challenges the assumption that frontier-quality AI requires cloud-scale compute.

items.title: Amazon closes in on $7.5bn deal to buy AI start-up Decart
items.summary: Amazon is nearing a $7.5bn acquisition of AI start-up Decart. The deal is reported to be aimed at helping AWS compete with Nvidia in the race for computing power.
items.why_it_matters: A major cloud provider acquiring an AI infrastructure start-up signals how aggressively the hyperscalers are moving to control AI compute capacity.

items.title: Cognition in Talks for $75 Billion Value With New Funding
items.summary: AI coding start-up Cognition is in talks to raise new funding at a $75 billion valuation, just two months after its last round, according to people familiar with the matter.
items.why_it_matters: The rapid valuation jump shows investors still pricing explosive growth into AI coding tools even as broader AI stocks sell off.

items.title: Amazon says attackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day in 11 minutes, but no patched release is available
items.summary: Amazon said attackers' AI agents independently discovered a zero-day vulnerability in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI tool, and used it to write files outside the intended storage directory in about 11 minutes. A fix has been merged into the source code, but no patched release is yet available.
items.why_it_matters: It is a concrete, timed example of autonomous AI agents finding and exploiting a real vulnerability faster than defenders could patch it.

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.summary: Week-long UN talks in Geneva aimed at agreeing a negotiating mandate for a binding treaty on autonomous weapons ("killer robots") collapsed after all-night negotiations failed to overcome Russian objections, despite most states wanting a binding mandate.
items.why_it_matters: The breakdown leaves the use of AI-driven autonomous weapons in warfare without any path toward binding international rules for now.

items.title: Trump Threatens to Bar U.S. Tech Firms From Building Data Centers Abroad
items.summary: President Trump threatened to bar U.S. tech companies from building data centers outside the United States and suggested he would tax those that do, though it was unclear how he would implement the plan.
items.why_it_matters: A threatened ban or tax on offshore AI data centers could reshape where major AI companies site their compute infrastructure.

items.title: California Nvidia Probe Covers Potential Criminal Law Violations
items.summary: California's investigation into whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors about it is also examining potential criminal violations of state law, raising the stakes for the chipmaker.
items.why_it_matters: A criminal dimension to the probe raises the legal exposure for the company that supplies the chips underpinning most of the AI industry.

items.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
items.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero sustainability goal as emissions from its AI data centers reach record levels.
items.why_it_matters: One of the largest AI infrastructure builders stepping back from a climate commitment could set a precedent for how the industry balances AI growth against emissions pledges.

items.title: Data center electricity use could double by 2030, IEA says
items.summary: The International Energy Agency says global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030 as the AI boom adds pressure to power grids worldwide.
items.why_it_matters: It quantifies, from an authoritative energy body, how much strain AI's growth is putting on global power infrastructure.

items.title: China Plans to Strengthen AI Token Standards in Computing Push
items.summary: China's National Data Administration plans to improve standards on the measurement and billing of AI tokens and on quality assessment, as Beijing guides the growth of its AI industry.
items.why_it_matters: Standardizing how AI compute and usage are measured and billed could shape how China's AI industry scales and competes globally.

items.title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini
items.summary: Google describes how Duplex, its voice-calling AI technology, has evolved and is now integrated into Gemini so it can place calls to businesses on a user's behalf.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a long-running Google voice-AI project being folded into Gemini as a mainstream agentic feature.

items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.summary: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in its Android and iOS apps, part of its effort to stop on-device AI agents such as Gemini and Siri from reading users' messages off the screen.
items.why_it_matters: A major privacy-focused messaging app is taking concrete product steps against OS-level AI agents reading on-screen content, highlighting a new privacy battleground.

items.title: Giving its AI more to read made T-Mobile's answers worse
items.summary: T-Mobile's CIO said giving its AI customer-service agents a large body of support documentation backfired because conflicting instructions sent the agents down wrong paths; a subsequent knowledge-graph approach was too slow and hard for the agents to navigate.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete, counterintuitive lesson for enterprises building AI agents: more context isn't automatically better and can degrade accuracy.

items.title: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
items.summary: AI coding tool maker Cursor told lawmakers it is considering phasing out Chinese-developed open-weight AI models because of geopolitical risk, according to a House report reviewed by CNBC.
items.why_it_matters: It shows geopolitical pressure directly influencing which underlying AI models a popular developer tool is willing to ship.
